templates.why_chosen: Star-rated, high-confidence 5-component figure that separates a solid data path (direct read/write to a shared Object) from a dashed control path (createObject/getObject calls) with an in-figure legend and five circled steps ordering the whole exchange.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw two symmetric peers around a shared object in the middle, label its access rights (WO/RO) directly on the box, and run the mediating monitor as a full-width band underneath; if you mark denied access with a red X, add it to the legend, unlike this figure.

templates.why_chosen: Star, rank-16 exemplar at only 5 components: two Trustlet peers flank an Object core marked with a red X, all resting on a Trusted Monitor band, a trusted-middle pattern at half the usual component count.
templates.what_to_learn: Mark a denied access path with one bold red X on the shared object rather than a caption, and give the figure a small top-right legend distinguishing solid data-path arrows from dashed control-path arrows; the weakness here is that the X itself has no legend entry, so give every ad hoc symbol one too.
